land.text: Asturias, annexed by the Kingdom of León in 924 when 'Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León'

successors.note: The Asturias page: 'Annexed by the Kingdom of León: 924'. León and Galicia had been re-united in 914 (page: 'León and Galicia in 914, Asturias later'). Cliopatria keeps an 'Asturias' row to 925.

capitals.name: Cangas de Onís
capitals.note: The Asturias page lists the capitals Cangas de Onís, San Martín del Rey Aurelio, Pravia and Oviedo without years; only Oviedo's 'circa 789' is dated. The years 718-788 are a bridging span for the three earlier seats; Pravia and San Martín del Rey Aurelio are not separated because the page gives no years.

capitals.name: Oviedo
capitals.note: 'Alfonso II chose his birthplace of Oviedo as the capital of the kingdom (circa 789).' The Alfonso III page adds 'In 909, Alfonso moved the seat of his government to Oviedo' and, after the 910 division, 'Fruela received Asturias with Oviedo as his capital'.

capitals.name: León
capitals.note: 'Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León' (924): the kingdom is annexed by León.

rulers.name: Favila
rulers.note: Reign years derived: Pelagius ends 737 (Asturias page), Alfonso I's 'Coronation: 739' (Alfonso I page) after Favila's 'premature death'.

rulers.name: Bermudo I
rulers.note: 'Mauregatus was succeeded by Bermudo I, Alfonso's cousin, who abdicated after his defeat at the Battle of the Burbia River'; Alfonso II was 'elected king on 14 September 791' (Alfonso II page). Added by reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25.

rulers.name: Alfonso II
rulers.note: 'Alfonso was subsequently elected king on 14 September 791', after the abdication of Bermudo I.

rulers.name: Fruela II
rulers.note: King of Asturias from the 910 division; king of León from 924 (page: 'Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León').

correction.text: the Asturian core where Pelagius founds the kingdom in 718 and defeats an Umayyad army at Covadonga in 722

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 724 and draws 78,284 km2 (Galicia, León, Cantabria) from the start. The page dates Galicia to 740 and León to 754 (Alfonso I page), so the founding core is the mountain heartland; the Asturias page gives 'Established: 718' and Covadonga 'In the summer of 722' but no boundary, so Asturias (province) is a reading, not a page boundary.

correction.text: Asturias, Cantabria and Galicia (reconquered 740) without León (conquered 754) and without northern Portugal (reached 773)

keyframe_review.note: 724-749, 78,285 km2. Valid from 739/740 only: the Alfonso I page dates the 'reconquest of Galicia' to 740 (Lugo and Tuy 'joined his domain') and the conquest of the city of León to 754, so León is removed here; northern Portugal is dated 773 (Asturias page), so Viana do Castelo is removed too. Cantabria is in from Alfonso I's accession in 739 (conf 1 in the ledger). 724-738 is replaced by the 718 keyframe. The Asturias infobox gives no area, so no ratio.

correction.text: 750-753: Asturias, Cantabria and Galicia without León; León (the city and its district) is added in 754

keyframe_review.note: 750-754, 78,644 km2. The shape holds León province, but the Alfonso I page says 'in 754, he conquered the City of León', and northern Portugal is only reached in 773 (Asturias page). From 754 León stands.

correction.text: 755-772: without the northern Portugal reached in 773; from 773 the Cliopatria shape stands

keyframe_review.note: 755-824, 78,716 km2. The Asturias page: 'In 773 the western frontier of the kingdom in Galicia was expanded into the northern part of modern-day Portugal'; Cliopatria already carries Viana do Castelo from 724. Stands from 773; 755-772 without northern Portugal. The same page's 'further expansion ... almost as far as Lisbon' under Alfonso II (791-842) is raiding (Lisbon 797/798), not annexation, so no southern addition is drawn.

correction.text: 825-867: the Cliopatria shape without the Porto, Aveiro and Viseu districts, which the Alfonso III page dates to 868 and 878

keyframe_review.note: 825-869, 123,130 km2: bbox south to 40.81 N and east to 1.78 W. The Alfonso II page: after the 825 victories of Narón and Anceo 'the repopulation of parts of Galicia, León, and Castile was started'; the Alfonso III page puts Porto in 868 ('Count Vimara Perez in 868 conquered Porto and resettled the district') and Viseu and Lamego in 878, so Porto, Aveiro and Viseu are removed until then. Zamora, Valladolid and the Duero are 'unverified: page budget' (the Alfonso I page speaks of a depopulated Duero frontier); La Rioja is doubtful (Ordoño I besieged the Banu Qasi fortress of Albelda in 859) but the Asturias page says Alfonso I 'pushed as far as La Rioja', so it stays.

870-877, 124,088 km2. Porto was taken in 868 (Alfonso III page); Aveiro and Viseu fringes appear about eight years before the page's 878 repopulation, a small excess at this resolution. Area has no infobox figure to compare with.

878-910, 128,718 km2, south to 39.90 N. The Alfonso III page: Braga, Viseu and Lamego repopulated in 878, Coimbra conquered in 879 ('conquered Porto and Coimbra in 867 and 879 respectively'); the Asturias page has the territory expanding 'further south' to the Mondego between 868 and 881. The shape matches within a year. Zamora and the Duero line are not dated by the pages opened (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: 'Fruela received Asturias with Oviedo as his capital' (the share of the third son after the division of 910)

keyframe_review.note: 911-921, 29,428 km2 around Burgos, La Rioja, Soria and Cantabria (50 of 56 cells of Burgos province), which is Castile and its borderlands, not Asturias. The Alfonso III page: after 910 'Fruela received Asturias with Oviedo as his capital' while García took León and Ordoño Galicia; Cliopatria's own León and Galicia rows for 911 already cover the Asturian heartland. Use the province of Asturias. The County of Castile page says Castile was a frontier lordship of León, but no page dates its transfer in 910 (notes).

correction.text: Fruela II's Asturias until the annexation by León in 924

keyframe_review.note: 922-925, 29,428 km2, the same eastern shape as 911. The Asturias page: 'Annexed by the Kingdom of León: 924'; 'Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León', so the state ends in 924, not 925. Same correction as 911 until 924.

region.text: the Asturian mountains of Pelagius, Cangas de Onís

ledger.note: 718: Pelagius founds the Kingdom of Asturias. Infobox 'Established: 718', first ruler 'Pelagius, 718-737'; the page names no boundary, so the core is the province of Asturias.

region.text: Cantabria, where Alfonso I 'held many lands'

ledger.note: 739: Alfonso I, 'son of Duke Peter of Cantabria', is crowned. The page says he 'held many lands in that region' and gives 'Coronation: 739' but is silent on when Cantabria joined the kingdom; Cliopatria draws it from 724.

740: Alfonso I reconquers Galicia. 'In 740, he took advantage of the Berber Revolt and led the reconquest of Galicia'; Lugo and Tuy, 'which Muslim forces had not occupied', joined his domain. Counterpart nobody: no Cliopatria shape covers Galicia then.

754: Alfonso I conquers the city of León. 'In 754, he conquered the City of León.' Counterpart: the Fihrid governors of al-Andalus (Yusuf al-Fihri), to whom the umayyad-caliphate dossier hands al-Andalus in 750 (its /ledger/93; that dossier ends in 750); Cliopatria's Umayyad row runs to 756. [Reviewer eu-12-a, 2026-10-25: counterpart changed from umayyad-caliphate.]

region.text: the northern part of modern-day Portugal

ledger.note: 773: the western frontier reaches northern Portugal. 'In 773 the western frontier of the kingdom in Galicia was expanded into the northern part of modern-day Portugal.' The districts are read from the phrase; no city is named.

789: Alfonso II makes Oviedo the capital. 'Alfonso II chose his birthplace of Oviedo as the capital of the kingdom (circa 789).' The Alfonso II page says only that the capital moved from Pravia to Oviedo, undated.

region.text: parts of Castile and León resettled from 825; the provinces are Cliopatria's reading

ledger.note: 825: after Narón and Anceo the Duero basin begins to be resettled. 'Thanks to these victories, the repopulation of parts of Galicia, León, and Castile was started.' The page names Castile but no towns; the Duero provinces are the reading of Cliopatria's 825 jump (to 123,130 km2).

868: Vimara Perez takes Porto. 'Count Vimara Perez in 868 conquered Porto and resettled the district.' The same page also says 'conquered Porto and Coimbra in 867 and 879 respectively', so the year is 867 or 868. Counterpart read as the emirate of Córdoba; the page says only 'conquered'.

region.text: the district between the Douro and the Mondego won and resettled in 878-879

ledger.note: 878: war with Córdoba on the Douro-Mondego frontier. 'Fighting occurred almost constantly between 875 and 883' (al-Mundir); in 878 Hermenegildo Gutiérrez's troops defeat Mohammad I's forces at Porto and the king wins the battle of Polvoraria. The zone is the land between the Douro and the Mondego.
878: Braga, Viseu and Lamego are repopulated. 'Christian forces repopulate Braga, Viseu, and Lamego' in 878; Braga was already inside from 773.

region.text: Coimbra and the land up to the Mondego

ledger.note: 879: Coimbra falls. 'conquered Porto and Coimbra in 867 and 879 respectively'; the Asturias page has the kingdom expanding to the Mondego between 868 and 881.
884: peace with Córdoba. 'In 884 Mohamed I and Alfonso III signed a peace.'

region.text: the whole kingdom of Alfonso III before the division

ledger.note: 910: the kingdom splits in three. 'When Alfonso III's sons forced his abdication in 910, the Kingdom of Asturias split into three separate kingdoms' (Asturias, León, Galicia); the Alfonso III page: 'García, became king of León; the second son, Ordoño, reigned in Galicia; Fruela received Asturias'.
910: Ordoño takes Galicia. 'The second son, Ordoño, reigned in Galicia.'

region.text: the kingdom of León of García I (Cliopatria 911) without Asturias and Galicia

ledger.note: 910: García takes León. 'His eldest son, García, became king of León.' The land is read as everything Cliopatria's León row for 911 holds beyond Asturias and Galicia.

region.text: the Burgos, Cantabria, Álava and La Rioja lands that Cliopatria labels Asturias in 911-925 (holder not dated by any page)

ledger.note: 910: the eastern lands (Castile, Cantabria, Álava, La Rioja) leave Asturias. The pages opened say only 'Fruela received Asturias'. The County of Castile page: Castile 'began as an eastern frontier lordship of the Kingdom of León' whose counties 'were initially administered and defended by León's monarchs', with 'the first count of a wider and more united Castile' Rodrigo in 850; no page dates the transfer in 910, so the land goes to León as a bridge (conf 1).
924: Asturias is annexed by León. 'Annexed by the Kingdom of León: 924'; 'Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León'.

924: the Kingdom of Asturias ends as Fruela II takes the crown of León. 'Fruela II of Asturias became king with his royal court in León.' The three kingdoms are 'reunited in 924 (León and Galicia in 914, Asturias later) under the crown of León'.

wars.name: Battle of Covadonga
wars.outcome: Asturian victory: 'In the summer of 722, Pelagius defeated an Umayyad army at the Battle of Covadonga.' No border moved.

wars.name: Reconquest of Galicia and León (Alfonso I)
wars.outcome: Asturias gains Galicia in 740 during the Berber Revolt and the city of León in 754.
wars.note: The Alfonso I page links the Galician campaign to the Berber Revolt without dating the revolt; it also says the frontier cities were abandoned, the 'Desert of the Duero'.

wars.name: Lisbon raid of Alfonso II
wars.outcome: A raid on Lisbon; no land was held. The Asturias page dates the Lisbon campaign to 797 ('spoils of war (campaign of Lisbon, 797)'); the Alfonso II page says Lisbon 'was captured and sacked by his troops in 798'.
wars.note: Years differ between the two pages; both are listed.

wars.name: Battles of Narón and Anceo
wars.outcome: Asturian victories: 'In 825, he defeated Saracen forces at Narón (near Ferrol)'; repopulation of parts of Galicia, León and Castile followed.

wars.name: Campaign of Albelda and Monte Laturce

zones.text: the fortress of Albelda in La Rioja and the heights of Monte Laturce

wars.outcome: Ordoño I defeats Musa ibn Musa at Monte Laturce outside Albelda, which Musa had recently fortified; Musa flees. No ground is recorded as held.
wars.note: The Asturias page dates the siege: 'In 859, Ordoño besieged the fortress of Albelda'. The Ordoño I page gives no year for the battle.

wars.name: Asturian-Cordoban war of Alfonso III

zones.text: the Douro-Mondego frontier: Porto 868, Viseu and Lamego 878, Coimbra 879

wars.outcome: 'Fighting occurred almost constantly between 875 and 883'; Hermenegildo Gutiérrez defeats Mohammad I at Porto and Alfonso wins at Polvoraria in 878; peace signed in 884 ('In 884 Mohamed I and Alfonso III signed a peace').
wars.note: The page does not date the three-year truce it mentions after 878.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists: the Duero and Mondego frontiers are zones of raiding and resettlement ('Desert of the Duero'); the 884 peace is not described as a line.

sources.title: Kingdom of Asturias
sources.note: Identity, 718, capitals, rulers, 773, Alfonso II to Lisbon, 910 split, 924 annexation. No area in the infobox.

sources.title: Alfonso II of Asturias
sources.note: 791 election, 798 Lisbon, 825 Narón and the repopulation of Castile, León and Galicia.

sources.title: Ordoño I of Asturias
sources.note: Reign 850-866; Albelda and Monte Laturce; repopulation of Tui, Astorga, León and Amaya (undated).

sources.title: County of Castile
sources.note: Castile as a frontier lordship of León; Rodrigo, first count of a wider Castile, 850; Fernán González 931.

sources.title: Alfonso III of Asturias
sources.note: Porto 868, Coimbra 879, 878 resettlements, peace 884, 909 seat, the 910 division among his sons.

notes: Cliopatria rows: the 911-925 'Kingdom of Asturias' shapes (29,428 km2 around Burgos, La Rioja, Soria and Cantabria) are not Asturias; marked wrong and replaced by the province of Asturias. The state ends in 924 (annexed by León), not 925. Not settled by the pages opened: who held Castile, Cantabria, Álava and La Rioja in 910-924 (the County of Castile page calls Castile 'an eastern frontier lordship of the Kingdom of León', first wider count Rodrigo in 850; Cliopatria has no Castile row before 961 and its León shape for 911 holds 1 of 56 Burgos cells, so the east is unowned in 911-960: the kingdom-of-castile or kingdom-of-leon dossier should start earlier); the date of Alfonso I's push 'as far as La Rioja'; the extent of the Duero frontier (Zamora, Valladolid, Palencia) before Alfonso III; Pravia and San Martín del Rey Aurelio as capitals (no years); Bermudo I (788-791) missing from the ruler list; the 901 attack on Zamora (the digest of the Alfonso III page is ambiguous about who attacked whom). Page conflicts: Porto 867 or 868 (both on the Alfonso III page); Lisbon 797 (Asturias page) or 798 (Alfonso II page); the Alfonso III page puts the move of the seat 'to Oviedo' in 909 although the Asturias page has Oviedo capital since about 789. Infobox area: the Asturias page gives none, so no ratio against Cliopatria. Gazetteer names used that exist: Asturias, Cantabria, León, Burgos, Palencia, Valladolid, Zamora (admin1); Viana do Castelo, Braga, Porto, Aveiro, Viseu (admin1 Portugal); 'Galicia (Spain)' (region). Pages budget: 5 of 5 used, plus the County of Castile page.
